question.text: An NPO client claims it qualifies as a Social Enterprise because '85% of its income has been applied for charitable purposes over the last 3 years'. Evaluating this for SSE eligibility, the SIA should note that:

answer.text: 85% income-application is the SEBI-ICDR primacy test and the NPO qualifies without further checks

85% is the Section 11 Income Tax threshold for tax exemption; it is NOT the SEBI-ICDR primacy test. An NPO must establish primacy of social intent via alignment with the 16 eligible activities and target underserved populations
85% is the CSR threshold under Section 135 — the NPO cannot claim SSE eligibility via this route
85% refers to the FCRA utilisation ratio and is unrelated to SSE

explanation.text: The Logic: The 85% threshold sits under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act 1961 and governs application of income by charitable trusts for tax-exemption purposes. It is separate from SEBI-ICDR eligibility, where the workbook states a Social Enterprise shall have at least 67% qualifying activities. An NPO must independently establish (a) engagement in at least one of the 16 eligible activities and (b) targeting of underserved populations, regardless of the 85% income-application figure. The Trap: Option A conflates tax and SSE regimes. Option C misattributes 85% to CSR under Section 135. Option D fabricates an FCRA ratio. Only B correctly distinguishes the two regimes. Note: Separate three tests in your scoping memo: legal form (Trust/Society/Section 8), IT exemption (12AB, 85% application, 80G), and SEBI-ICDR primacy (16 activities + target + 67% qualifying-activities test). This prevents cross-regime confusion during fieldwork.
